transcript: Last night, I saw one of the most unhinged comedy sets I've ever seen. Or perhaps I should say anti-comedy set. As his alter ego Jack Tucker, Zach Zucker hilariously stumbles through around 75 minutes of bits which feel like 90% build up, 10% the joke itself, and 100% ridiculous. The jerky, self-deprecating stop and start of almost every joke is intentional and on brand for Zach’s stage persona Jack. The comedy is in the character work, the pacing of the show, and how derailed you’d consider it relative to a standard comedy set. The jokes themselves almost don't matter, it's the chaos surrounding the jokes that make the show memorable. But don't be fooled by the seemingly spontaneous interactions and mishaps. The precision, particularly in Zach's physicality along with the integration of relentless sound cues, I imagine have been carefully crafted and rehearsed. Which is why to me, the show feels just as much of a theater piece as it does a comedy show. If you're in the marker for a good laugh or something nontraditional, Jack Tucker is hosting his “Comedy Standup Hour” at the Vineyard Theater every night through this Saturday the 14th.
